title: Seeds, threads and work limits, solver by solver

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: An interview answer says: "To make Gurobi deterministic, set Method=2." A colleague's runs of one MIP with Threads fixed at 8 and every other parameter at its default already repeat exactly. What is the accurate correction?

options.text: Method=2 selects barrier for the root LP; the runs already repeat without it
options.says: Right: the page's default and fixed-thread runs repeated; Method=2 repeated too, on another path.

options.text: Method=2 is still needed, as the runs repeat now because the machine is idle
options.says: Gurobi's default with a fixed thread count repeated on the page; machine load matters to time limits, not here.

options.text: Method=2 selects barrier, the algorithm Gurobi keeps repeatable across threads
options.says: The page says Method=2 is not what makes Gurobi repeat; the default run repeated without it.

options.text: Method=2 sets Gurobi's random seed, which is why the runs already repeat
options.says: The seed is the Seed parameter, and Method was left at its default; the page says Method picks the LP algorithm.

origin.section: Gurobi: Deterministic for a Fixed Thread Count, and Method=2 Is Barrier

questions.stem: A service sets num_search_workers = 6, random_seed = 3 and max_deterministic_time = 10, and its nightly plans differ. Which change makes them repeat?

options.text: Rename it to num_workers = 6, since the old name is read as a single worker
options.says: The old name is still read; the page's four workers under it raced, and under the new name too.

options.text: Swap the work limit for a 60-second time limit, so all six workers stop together
options.says: A clock limit stops each run at a different point; the page shows it adds differences.

options.text: Lower the work limit to 2, so the six workers stop before their paths split
options.says: The page's four workers under a limit of 2 still ended at different plans.

options.text: Set interleave_search = True, so the six workers' tasks run in fixed batches
options.says: Right: four workers differed under both names and repeated once the search was interleaved.

origin.section: CP-SAT: num_workers Is the New Name, and Only Interleaving Makes Workers Repeat

questions.stem: A test file solves three MIPs with HiGHS through MathOpt in one process: the first with threads 1 in HiGHS's own options, the second with threads 4, the third with threads 1. What happens to the second solve?

options.text: It runs on 4 threads, since each solve hands its own options to HiGHS
options.says: The page says the first HiGHS solve fixes the count for the whole process.

options.text: It runs on 1 thread without a word, since HiGHS ignores a count it cannot change
options.says: A different count is not ignored; lesson 4.2.4's run reported an INTERNAL error.

options.text: It fails, since the first HiGHS solve fixed the thread count for the whole process
options.says: Right: the first solve fixed the count; decide it once per process, or run each count in its own process.

options.text: It fails, since MathOpt refuses a thread count for HiGHS however it is passed
options.says: MathOpt refuses the common threads field, but accepts the count in HiGHS's own options.

origin.section: HiGHS: A Seed, a Thread Count Fixed per Process, and a Node Limit for Work
